Hypercasual Teardown · Mobile web adaptation

Aquapark.io

The quickest route is the one you dare to leave the slide for.

A bright water race turns steering into a spatial gamble: stay inside the flume, shove a rival, or fly across the gap toward a lower section. A readable landing makes the shortcut feel earned. A late, unexplained loss breaks that bargain.

16starting places shownSlide → flydefining transitionbug.gamescomplete free base planned
01 / Product context

A small gesture, a very large reach.

Aquapark.io sells an immediately legible fantasy: overtake people on a giant waterslide, including by jumping over the route itself.

Cassette LLC is credited by publisher VOODOO in its developer spotlight. The original iOS release is listed as February 28, 2019. This report studies two creator recordings of older mobile play; it does not treat them as a walkthrough of the current app.

On October 6, 2026, the US App Store showed 4.6/5 from roughly 2.8 million ratings, while Google Play showed 3.8/5 from roughly 1.48 million reviews and 100 million-plus downloads. These are storefront signals with different populations, not a controlled comparison or a revenue estimate.

There is no usable Metacritic critic aggregate: its iOS page lists zero critic reviews and a pending score. No matching Steam listing was located in the targeted search, so no Steam review or player-count claim is made.

A 2019 review by Carl Fisher at the publication now called GRAVENOISE rated version 2.1 at 2/10, describing intuitive controls but repetitive content and intrusive ads. The dated ACCM review also singled out ad interruptions. Those opinions identify a useful adaptation problem; their small-content descriptions do not describe the later shops and environments illustrated here.

Sources: VOODOO developer spotlight · US App Store · Google Play · Metacritic · Fisher’s 2019 review · ACCM’s 2019 review.

02 / The defining decision

A corner is also a launch site.

The valuable choice is not merely left versus right. It is whether to keep the route’s safety or trade it for a shorter, less certain line through space.

The shortcut bargain

Hold the flumeStay on a visible surface; manage turns, obstacles and nearby racers.Less exposure · more route to travel
Leave and re-enterFind a reachable lower segment, steer through the gap and land on it.Time saved · landing risk
Commit to the poolBypass the remaining slide and aim for the actual finish volume.Largest skip · smallest recovery margin

This is a qualitative model of the decisions. It is not a measured probability curve; the source physics and collision tolerances are unavailable.

Forward motion carries the burden

The race presents a behind-the-avatar camera, a progress strip and an ordinal place. Steering is the apparent main control; the recordings do not expose finger coordinates. The avatar can leave an open-topped flume and later occupy a lower segment, so a faithful adaptation needs real elevated route geometry and off-route flight.

Rank provides a fast consequence, while the visible next section gives the player something to aim at. The camera must preserve that relationship through takeoff. A beautiful wide shot that hides the reachable surface would weaken the action.

The route should become clearer when the player takes the risk.

03 / Read the consequence

The landing is the proof.

A shortcut needs a visible contact, a regained route and continued control. A score burst alone is not enough.

The inspected landing shows a bright exhaust trail and two reward messages. Nearby browser checks show the same run continuing on the slide. This supports the intended takeoff-to-re-entry experience, while leaving the exact launch impulse, steering strength, landing bonus calculation and perfect-alignment threshold open.

The adaptation should distinguish a clean re-entry from a graze. On a clean contact, water spray, a short avatar settle and a concise reward label explain success. The player must immediately regain steering; extended celebration cannot steal the next corner.

A glider changes the flight opportunity. It should give a wider reachable envelope, while preserving aim and collision consequences. It must not become an automatic teleport to first place.

04 / Interference

Other racers give the line a cost.

Bumping makes the safe route contested. Shark starts briefly exaggerate that contest into a power fantasy.

The supplied analyses describe lateral shoves, brown crate obstacles, chevron speed pads and a short shark transformation. Actual images confirm knockout feedback and shark appearances. They do not independently establish crate contact resolution, pad color, invulnerability, speed multipliers or bot teleportation. Those systems remain in the target inventory, with their interactions specified as design choices.

For the web game, all 15 rivals should occupy the same simulated route space as the player. Small variations in steering, risk preference and start reaction create visible race texture. A rival may take its own shortcut; it may not silently respawn ahead to cancel the player’s advantage. Rank must be a consequence of simulated progress and finish order.

05 / Failure and recovery

A miss should teach the next attempt.

The failure screen reports distance and knockouts. The reason for the miss must be visible before that screen replaces the scene.

Open water and the terminal pool are visually similar but have opposite meanings. Ground, pool rim and flume side walls need distinct collision feedback. The target should leave the camera on the failed landing long enough to reveal what was missed, then offer an immediate free retry.

The original presents a rewarded revive. Its actual restore point and retained rewards are not sufficiently established. The proposed base game instead retries the same authored stage and layout. It preserves banked coins, collection and campaign progress; it discards the unfinished race ledger. This creates a concrete second attempt without requiring a commercial interruption.

The local-library pilot supports one narrow borrowing: Flip Trickster’s visible failed pose followed by a reset at the same spatial challenge. Keep that causal continuity. Do not import its flip controls, scoring or campaign.

Adaptation decision: make the cause of a miss legible, then return control in a new attempt. A free retry is part of the complete base game.
06 / The return loop

Race mastery funds identity.

Choose a line→Finish the race→Bank coins→Unlock a look→Try the next stage

Three prices, one expressive collection

The shop offers Common, Rare and Legend categories. The visible prices are 300, 700 and 1.50k coins in the respective inspected screens. The reports also describe a different 5.0k Legend price in another recording, but its actual Legend screen is not delivered. Keep the price context separate; there is no evidence for a universal cross-version tariff.

Collection is a change of appearance, not demonstrated permanent power progression. The web adaptation should preserve equal handling across skins and let players preview, equip and cancel without spending. A purchase must reveal a newly owned item and deduct the advertised amount once. Duplicate protection and a disabled completed tier are explicit target choices, because the native refusal and duplicate rules remain unknown.

07 / Escalation

New scenery needs new reading.

Theme changes punctuate repeat races. They should also change the spatial questions.

The material reaches from early tropical tracks to City flight, Winter and a Candyland lobby. The wider reported route includes blossom gardens, forts, dunes and oasis settings, plus later Hollywood and Octopus previews. Those latter identities and gates are not all independently pictured. Their full scope is retained as explicit design space, rather than compressed into an early-level demonstration.

Teach one relation at a time: first a reachable lower turn, then a boost before a bend, then a glider with more than one viable re-entry. Later levels can combine narrow contacts, moving rivals and alternative pool approaches. Each authored stage needs a safe completion line and at least one intentional risk opportunity.

Worlds should change silhouette, height arrangement and route rhythm. Color swaps alone would not justify a long tour.

08 / Mobile web direction

Protect the gamble. Remove the interruptions.

The complete free game should offer a whole tour, a functioning collection and repeatable races in a single offline-capable HTML. Its strongest retention mechanism is a better second attempt.

Keep elevated 3D flumes, lateral steering, player-directed flight, contested re-entry and a real finish pool. Translate them to one-handed touch with the finger below the meaningful landing area. Remove forced ad gates, rating popups during results and offers that interrupt a missed jump. Provide clear Settings access between races and during pause.

A short contextual prompt can explain the first meaningful drag and the first lip exit. A compact progress strip can locate the player relative to the finish and leading rival. Both are hypotheses informed by Bloom Brain references, not claims that a Roblox economy belongs inside a waterslide race.

Make “I can land that next time” the reason to return.

The Build layer below freezes the connected scope and testable invariants while leaving numerical feel tuning to a builder who plays the result. It is a specification, not a playable game or a claim that implementation tests have already passed.

Implementation handoff / Static, readable, self-contained

Build layer

Complete-game specification: ready with named evidence limits. HTML delivery: structure, embedded evidence and responsive reading verified. No game has been built.

Basis labels used below: Observed = independently inspected pixels or bounded browser states; Reported = supplied analysis or archive statement not independently replayed; External = dated primary documentation; Designed = target choice or optional tuning example. A checked number does not certify its formula.

Short prompt for this game

Build a complete mobile-first water-slide racer for bug.games as one offline-capable HTML: auto-slide through elevated open 3D flumes against 15 simulated rivals, steer by dragging, deliberately exit a lip, steer flight toward a lower segment or the terminal pool, and make clean re-entry visibly regain control. Include shoves, crates, speed pads, glider pickups and freely earned shark starts; deliver the full 11-world, 55-stage tour, replayable stages, cosmetic coin collection, clear failure and immediate free retry, with persistent progress. Keep route choices and simulated finish order honest. Use original coherent assets; do not reuse the report’s reference screenshots as game assets. Add complete EN/RU UI, independent persisted music and SFX sliders, and the guarded platform, analytics and planned-extras boundary below. Read the rule, design-space and acceptance tables; inspect their embedded figures. Tune unknown physics through real phone play, record your choices, and report which designed cases pass. The staged work order is not permission to stop at a demo.

Complete loop, timing and tuning space

Design a normal race for roughly 25–60 seconds in early stages and 40–90 seconds in later layouts; these are target pacing bands, not timings measured from edited recordings. One corner/re-entry choice should fit within a few seconds of continuous control. Menus must not be required between free retries. A 20-minute session can traverse several races and encounter the shop; it need not complete the full tour.

An optional first economy calibration is 100 coins for first place, decreasing smoothly toward a 40-coin finish floor, plus 10 per credited KO and bounded landing rewards. Try prices 300 / 700 / 1500 as the first target tariff. This is a Designed tuning example, not a mandatory balance freeze or reconstructed native formula. Record the chosen formula, test time to first unlock through ordinary play, and ensure repeated failed races cannot create a free coin exploit. All normal earnings and purchases must reconcile in the visible ledger.

Avoid a perfect full-path predictor that removes aiming. Test under finger/HUD occlusion.

Suggested build order: establish one real 3D route with all movement states; connect rivals, contacts and finish ledger; exercise failure and collection; author and play the full tour; add presentation/audio/settings; integrate platform boundary and run all cases. This is sequencing, not a reduced delivery scope.

Core statements and the mobile bridge

  1. C1: choose safety versus a shorter airborne route; a valid re-entry changes race position and permits the next steering choice.
  2. C2: sharing a surface with rivals makes line choice consequential; a shove can improve position but can also send the player off route.
  3. C3: flight tools alter the reachable route without removing aiming; a miss reveals the surface or pool the player failed to reach.
  4. C4: completed races create persistent progress and expressive purchases; retry preserves what was already earned.

Local archive pilot: one accepted causal mechanism

Read-only queries were jump landing trajectory risk preview and failure retry cause readable feedback. The available archive produced Flip Trickster, Hoop World 3D, Slice It All, Helix Jump, Hark the Ghoul and Bowmasters among the first query’s leads; Golf Orbit, Ball Blast, Clue Hunter, Draw Joust, Draw to Smash, Flip Trickster and Gun Head Run among the second. Only Flip Trickster, Helix Jump and Bowmasters were shortlisted and inspected in detail.

Archive reference images illustrate the accepted pilot mechanism only. They are not Aquapark evidence or target-game assets. No new empirical effectiveness result is claimed.

Art, camera and animation direction

Signal / functionTarget treatment / asset statusPhone and motion check
Flume / water / poolOriginal procedural low-poly geometry, glossy wet center, readable rim and distinct terminal-pool boundary. Pale aqua/green water language; per-world silhouettes.Pool must read as finish while surrounding water reads as failure. Confirm with sound off and a finger on screen.
Avatars / glider / sharkOriginal consistent rounded low-poly family; color/shape-readable bot outfits, unmistakable wing span and shark phase. Source meshes are reference-only.Player silhouette visible over both pale Winter and pink Candyland; tool mesh never hides imminent contact.
Hazard / boost / pickupCrate silhouette, directional chevrons, suspended wings; separate shape and color cues. No decorative object with identical gameplay shape.Find the next steerable opening at race speed; effects do not cover it.
Camera and motion phasesOn-flume follow → widened flight view → touchdown settle → restored chase; pool dive → fixed result; miss → cause view → retry. Exact durations Designed, iterated through play.Avoid snap/lag that changes apparent input direction. Keep contact visible under motion and rapid camera changes.
Assets / creditsAll needed art/audio is currently a brief, not supplied ready assets. Generate or author original assets; if sourcing files, verify each exact licence and keep ASSETS.md internally before embedding.One coherent family, no temporary missing placeholders in completed base. No source screenshots in the playable game; report embedding is analysis provenance, not a licence grant.

Audio event sheet and music brief

Original game audio has not been heard through an audio-capable inspection tool. Creator commentary and possible added music further limit matching. The following is a Designed cue-role brief; no measured BPM, millisecond envelope, native timbre or ready audio file is claimed.

Trigger / roleDesigned layers, mix and readinessAsset status / source interval
Sliding / paceSoft looping water wash, modest speed-dependent intensity; lower priority than landing and failure. Stop on pause/terminal state.Missing; original/procedural approximation. No independently heard interval.
Lip exit / flightBrief airy whoosh into a quiet wind layer; expose takeoff without hiding feedback. Different texture while glider attached.Missing; procedural/original. Visual route/wing figures only.
Rival contact / KOShort rounded impact; distinct higher accent only on credited KO. Use variation and voice limits so a shark cluster does not become a harsh wall of sounds.Missing; original synthesis permitted, no source match certified.
Crate / pad / pickupDull wooden contact; compact rising boost cue; lightweight wing-unfurl cue. Immediate trigger, no music-bus dependency.Missing; three distinct designed roles.
Landing / Perfect LandWater contact transient; brighter accent only for clean landing. Briefly duck continuous water/wind so contact reads, then restore smoothly.Missing; synchronization must be tested against actual target contact.
Finish / fail / unlock / purchaseFinish splash plus compact celebration; miss splash/thud with no mocking voice; world unlock and cosmetic reveal have distinct short rewards.Missing; user gesture unlock and independent SFX mute required.
Music: menu / race / resultLight playful percussion and plucked/synth melody; race pulse leaves room for water and impacts. Short repeatable phrases, restrained density; result accent transitions into menu loop. No narrator track.Missing original score; choose tempo through target play, record loop boundary and transitions. Do not use a SFX tool to promise a complete soundtrack.

Test that loops do not stack after restart, all audio pauses on document hide, music/SFX controls truly affect separate buses, and both zero settings yield silence. Original-audio fidelity remains unverified even if the target mix is successful.

bug.games: publication and runtime boundary

The official connected SDK documentation was read on October 6, 2026. Use the platform’s SDK contract, not a guessed web API or an ad integration. The complete game remains playable when platform connection is absent. The report itself makes no SDK calls.

{
  "title": "[original water-racer title]",
  "hook": "Leave the slide, land a shortcut, beat the field.",
  "mood": "playful",
  "minutes": 2,
  "inputs": ["touch", "mouse"],
  "players": "1",
  "coop": false,
  "controls": [
    {"key": "Drag", "action": "Steer on the slide and in the air"},
    {"key": "Pause", "action": "Pause the race and open Settings"}
  ],
  "moments": [
    "first_race_started", "first_shortcut_landed", "first_ko",
    "first_pool_finish", "first_cosmetic_unlocked", "first_glider_used",
    "first_world_unlocked", "tour_completed"
  ],
  "products": []
}

These are draft values for documented metadata fields; validate the publishing schema and its exact moments representation when implementing. The 2-minute metadata estimate is a session entry expectation, not full-tour length. All eight proposed moment IDs must be declared consistently with calls to progress.moment; do not invent unregistered moments.

  1. Start the offline core first. If window.parent === window, skip the platform import. In an embedded platform context, conditionally import the exact own-origin path /sdk/bloomplay.js, apply the documented embedded guard and await bloomplay.init. Handle rejection; a timer alone is not proof of connection.
  2. Call loaded() once the game is visibly controllable. Use gameplayStart() at actual active-race entry and gameplayStop() on pause, document hide, result, failure or purchase interruption. Track current gameplay state if initialization is pending and reconcile after it resolves; do not emit duplicate edges.
  3. Call each declared progress.moment at its actual first qualifying stable boundary. Use native calls for platform lifecycle/moments. Do not re-send automatic bp_page_view or gameplay events through custom analytics.
  4. Keep core game saves device-local and versioned. If adding optional SDK save synchronization, follow documented save behavior and conflict rules, never erase a valid local save because a service read fails. Settings remain device-local.
  5. Use SDK catalog and entitlement data for extras. Offline/unavailable states keep racing available. No invented ad API, payout rate, revenue estimate, or game-origin direct request to platform services.

Analytics plan: only questions about this race

Custom eventExact stable trigger / propertiesQuestion / boundary
route_choiceLip exit committed: stage_id, world_id, attempt_id, tool, route_branch, progress_band.Where do players choose risk? Do not log every frame or raw pointer coordinates.
shortcut_resultFlight resolves: success/miss/graze, target_type, stage_id, tool, progress_gain_band.Which intended shortcuts are legible and controllable? One event per flight, linked to attempt.
race_outcomeCommitted terminal state: stage_id, finish_rank or fail_cause, KO_count, elapsed_active_ms, tool, attempt_number.Do losses cluster around pool rims, specific contacts or tools? Exclude paused time.
retry_startedFree retry actually starts a new countdown: previous_failure_cause, stage_id, retry_delay_band.Do players return quickly after a understandable miss? Cannot prove learning by this event alone.
cosmetic_unlockAtomic local purchase succeeds: tier, local_price, owned_count, races_since_first_start.Can ordinary play reach a meaningful look? No personal profile/name or platform purchase duplicated here.
guide_stepContextual prompt first shown/dismissed/fulfilled: step_id, stage_id, action_result.Does RB01 help discover steering/exit? Compare sessions fairly; do not claim before/after causation without a test.
extra_previewAvailable optional preview opened/closed: product_id, preview_action.Is the extra discoverable without interrupting a race? Native purchase/entitlement events remain platform-owned.

Use analytics.track only after a successful platform connection; unavailable analytics must never block a terminal transition. Aggregate stage/attempt properties without player names, touch traces or personal identifiers. Moment firsts and repeat custom events serve different questions; avoid using both as duplicate counters for the same dashboard metric.

Publication checklist for the future build: one self-contained playable HTML plus validated platform metadata; truthful thumbnail/title; verified original/licensed assets; complete EN/RU interface; all free systems reachable; no external runtime dependency for offline core; platform connection and unavailable branches exercised. No upload or publication is performed in this task.

Acceptance cases frozen before implementation

These are expected cases, not executed game tests. “Observed” below applies only to the stated source component; setup, touch actions and designed numerical tolerances must be exercised on the finished game. Debug teleport/accelerated unlocks may inspect edge states but cannot replace ordinary-play progression or balance checks.

Additional processed source states and coverage limits

The other supplied frames were inspected but not promoted as required figures: A at 16 seconds is an obstructing facecam, 45 a fading failure, 94 a pool-dive state, 112 a shark start, 194 a wing pickup ahead, 290 a lobby, 307 a Polar Bear sliding with exhaust, 341 a blurred result, and 351 an owned Rare-shop state. B at 826 seconds shows the 468-coin result with K.O. 0. Some of these are already represented by related figures; none proves the planned caption simply because its capture completed.

Browser supplementary observations at A 151.719 seconds show 12th place and KO 2 on the flume; at 156.721 seconds show continued flume sliding in 1st place; at 187.387 seconds show a 163-coin, KO 4 result with bank 503. These observations are retained in internal notes, not delivered as replacement still assets. Intervening touch inputs, exact air duration and reward formula remain unknown.

Requests and hashes were checked by the intake helper: 76 recorded files verified, no integrity errors. Semantic review independently classified all 27 images. Both response recovery files preserve the analysis text; their existence is not new independent evidence. No Gemini rerun occurred. No other run was mixed in.

Receiving-model image access was checked locally by extracting/decoding the embedded figures and opening representative gameplay and donor pixels during authoring. A separate receiving agent was not invoked, so no independent receiving-agent comprehension test is claimed.
